featured_reviews.name: Aditi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
After looking at the 5-star reviews, I visited this doctor for my mother’s left leg pain. Unfortunately, our experience was disappointing. The doctor is polite in speech but seems very money-minded.

During the first visit, he charged ₹1500 (normal fees), but strongly insisted on getting a Doppler test done through a specific lab. He even called the lab in front of us and mentioned sending the patient directly, which clearly felt like a commission-based referral. This was despite us clearly stating that we wanted to do the test at another known place. He claimed that ultrasounds done elsewhere would not be reliable. The lab he suggested charged ₹6000, while we got the same test done at our known place for ₹5000.

As instructed, we shared the report with him on WhatsApp, but there was no response. Later, my brother personally visited the clinic just to show the reports (the patient was not present). Ideally, this should have been free since it was only for report discussion, but he still charged ₹1000. On top of that, he again recommended another radiologist by sharing a specific name and phone number.

Overall, this was the most money-minded and disappointing experience I’ve had with a doctor.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hello! I really feel sorry for patients like you.It is unfortunate that when a correct clinical diagnosis was made and appropriate steps were taken to prevent you from being misled, the response is criticism rather than appreciation. You previously did an incorrect scan elsewhere, which you don't have anything to say about. Now, when a correct scan was suggested after clinical examination, and a correct diagnosis was made, here you are making allegations without even having visited for the follow up consultation and understanding the problem. Let's get the facts clear!

The reason a specific centre was suggested, was to prevent a repeat of an incorrect investigation (like you did before). Prior to consulting me, a venous Doppler had already been done, while your mother’s clinical presentation was not sciatica or venous problem, but strongly suggestive of arterial insufficiency (ischemic pain). A venous Doppler would never diagnose this condition.

The recommendation was therefore for a proper arterial Doppler, done by a senior, reliable radiologist, with whom precise requirements could be clearly communicated. The phone call was made only to ensure the correct study was performed this time — not for any financial reason. I have no commission arrangements, nor do I compel patients to visit any particular center. You were always free to choose where to do the test, which you ultimately did — and the scan confirmed the arterial block, exactly as suspected clinically. (which you should rather appreciate for spot on clinical diagnosis!)

Suggesting accuracy over repetition of wrong tests is called responsible medical practice, not “money-mindedness”.

At no point were you instructed to seek treatment or consultation over WhatsApp. Medical opinions are not given casually over messages.

Your brother later visited the clinic for formal report discussion and guidance, which constitutes a consultation. Doctors do not charge for “presence of the patient” — they charge for professional expertise, time, and responsibility involved in interpreting reports and guiding next steps. This is the same principle by which professionals in any field are paid for their work. Do you or your family members work for free? or ever say to your boss that you don't want payment for a particular month? or a 50% less salary this month would be okay?

If there was any financial difficulty, it could have been communicated. We offer concessions, fee waivers, and charity OPD options for genuinely needy patients. We doctors do that.

It is disappointing that sincere efforts to guide a patient onto the correct diagnostic path are interpreted otherwise. Medicine requires trust in clinical judgment, not assumptions about intent.

I genuinely wish your mother good health. However, when decision-makers are like you who lack trust and respect for sound medical advice, it may indeed be better to continue with whose approach you are more comfortable with and keep on doing investigation after investigations. All the best! 👍🏻

featured_reviews.review_text:
I would have not posted any review and kept the frustration within myself but as per the PROTOCOL of ANSSI Wellness I have to post a review. So here it is...

THE TREATMENT COST (The "Fish Market" Strategy):
Be warned: ANSSI Wellness quotes prices based on what they think they can get from you, not on a fixed medical rate. I met a patient who was quoted 1.2 Lakhs, but after he refused, they kept calling and reducing the price until he enrolled for just 40K. This is not a professional clinic; it’s a bazaar. They use three standard machines (Hydrotherapy, Spinal Decompression, and IFT/TENS/Laser) which are available at local clinics for significantly less. They charge 80K for what would likely cost 30K elsewhere.

MANAGEMENT & THE "UPFRONT" TRAP:
Clinic Manager Deepak is extremely persistent. Despite informing him of my upcoming travel, he used sales tactics to ensure I paid 40K upfront and joined sooner. I quickly became dissatisfied with the inconsistency; my first doctor resigned within a week, and the replacement physio gave opposite advice. I felt trapped because I had already paid 40K. When I tried to delay the balance payment to finish the sessions I had already funded, Deepak insisted on full payment to access a "Revised Protocol." This "Protocol" is just a fancy buzzword—there was no change in treatment; it was simply a tactic to squeeze the remaining money out of me.

UNPROFESSIONAL CONDUCT & LACK OF HYGIENE:
The clinic's "premium" pricing does not reflect its maintenance. The toilet flush and wash basin outlet remained broken and unrepaired from my first day to my last. It is shocking that a clinic charging such high fees is so stingy about basic hygiene and repairs.

Furthermore, Deepak’s behavior is appalling:
He frequently interrupted my sessions to ask the doctor "How much more time?"—pressuring the physio to rush my treatment.

After telling me it was fine to take a travel break before I joined, he later blamed that same break for my pain aggravation, simply because he already had my money.

The clinic is understaffed; if a physio is on leave, sessions are cancelled as there is no backup.

THE STAFF:
The saving grace is the medical staff. Dr. Faisal was honest and upright. Dr. Shikha is an amazing, dedicated physiotherapist; it is solely because of her care that I finished my sessions rather than walking away and losing my money. Hemangi Velari (Receptionist) and Arman Sankat (Technician) are also polite and supportive.

ADVICE TO PATIENTS:
1) Compare prices elsewhere for these machines first; you will save thousands.
2) NEVER pay upfront. Pay per session so you aren't held hostage by Deepak’s "protocols."

Many people ignore strange sensations in their legs until the pain becomes severe. But your body often gives warning signs much earlier.
If you experience tingling in legs, burning sensation in legs, or a constant pins and needles sensation, it could be a sign of nerve pain in leg caused by irritation or compression of nerves.
One of the most common reasons behind these symptoms is sciatica nerve pain, where the sciatic nerve gets irritated in the lower back or hip. This can lead to leg numbness causes, tingling in legs, and sometimes even leg weakness causes. Many people also experience a burning sensation in legs that travels down the thigh or calf.
In some cases, nerve compression symptoms can develop due to prolonged sitting, poor posture, disc irritation, or tight muscles. When the nerve is irritated, it can produce sensations like pins and needles sensation, tingling in legs, or sharp nerve pain in leg.
Another possible reason for these symptoms is peripheral neuropathy symptoms, where nerves become sensitive and start sending abnormal signals like burning sensation in legs, numbness, or weakness.
Sometimes people also notice leg swelling causes along with heaviness and discomfort, which may increase pressure around nerves and worsen sciatica symptoms or nerve compression symptoms.
The good news is that many of these problems can improve with proper physiotherapy for nerve pain.

At first glance, it looks like this person is simply strapped to a moving table... but what if I told you this machine is actually creating space inside the spine to help relieve back pain and sciatica?
What you're seeing is Spinal Decompression Therapy, a specialized non-surgical treatment commonly used for people suffering from chronic lower back pain, sciatica, bulging discs, herniated discs, and certain degenerative spinal conditions.
So how does it work?
The motorized table applies a gentle, controlled pulling force to the lumbar spine (lower back). This creates a process called **decompression**, where the vertebrae are slightly separated, reducing pressure on the spinal discs and nearby nerves.
Why is this important?
🦴 Reduces Disc Pressure
Spinal discs act as shock absorbers between your vertebrae. When a disc bulges or herniates, it can press on nearby nerves and cause pain, numbness, or tingling down the leg. Decompression may help reduce this pressure.
💧 Improves Nutrient Exchange
Unlike many tissues in the body, spinal discs have a very limited blood supply. The gentle stretching and relaxation cycles help encourage the movement of water, oxygen, and nutrients into the discs, supporting their health and recovery.
While spinal decompression can be beneficial for the right patient, it isn't a one-size-fits-all solution. A proper assessment is always important to determine the root cause of your pain.

⚖️ MYTH vs FACT

❌ Myth: Every Slip Disc Requires Surgery

✅ Fact: Most patients improve without surgery.

A slip disc diagnosis can be worrying, but surgery is not the answer for everyone. In fact, most patients recover successfully with medications, physiotherapy, lifestyle modifications, and guided rehabilitation.

Surgery is generally reserved for selected situations such as persistent severe pain, progressive neurological weakness, or loss of bladder and bowel control.

The most important principle in spine care is to treat the patient's symptoms and clinical condition—not just the MRI report.

If you are experiencing back pain, leg pain, or have concerns about your MRI findings, a proper clinical evaluation can help determine the best treatment approach.

🦴 *SPINE TIP OF THE WEEK*

*THE 10-SECOND SCOLIOSIS CHECK*
*Could Your Child Have a Curved Spine?*

Many children with scoliosis have *no pain at all*, which is why it often goes unnoticed until the curve becomes more obvious.

The good news? A simple 10-second check at home can help identify early warning signs.

👀 *What to look for:*
✅ One shoulder higher than the other
✅ Uneven waistline
✅ One side of the rib cage appearing more prominent
✅ Leaning to one side while standing
✅ Uneven posture in photographs

💡 *Try this simple test:*
Ask your child to stand with feet together, bend forward, and touch their toes while you observe from behind.

Early detection can make a significant difference, especially during growth spurts between *10–16 years of age*.

Remember:
👉 Not every uneven shoulder means scoliosis.
👉 But if you notice any of these signs, it's worth getting the spine evaluated.

A quick 10-second check today could make a lifelong difference tomorrow.

📤 Please share this with parents, teachers, coaches, school groups, and anyone involved in children's health and development. Early awareness matters. 😊

🏃‍♂️ Spine Tip of the Week | The Runner's Paradox

Many runners have excellent cardiovascular fitness and endurance, but running alone may not fully protect against age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia), reduced strength, or declining bone health.

While running trains your heart, strength training helps protect your muscles, bones, joints, and spine.

Benefits of regular strength training for runners:
✅ Improved running efficiency
✅ Better spine support
✅ Reduced injury risk
✅ Stronger muscles and bones
✅ Prevention of age-related muscle loss

A simple goal: For every 3–4 running sessions per week, include at least 2 strength-training sessions. Even 20 minutes twice weekly can make a meaningful difference.

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we encourage runners and active individuals to focus on both endurance and strength for long-term spine health and injury prevention.

🦴 Spine Tip of the Week | Text Neck Syndrome

Do you spend several hours daily looking at your phone, laptop, or tablet?

Prolonged screen use can place excessive stress on the cervical spine, leading to a condition commonly known as **Text Neck Syndrome**. As the head tilts forward, the load on the neck muscles and cervical discs increases significantly, contributing to neck pain, shoulder stiffness, headaches, poor posture, and upper back discomfort.

A simple habit can help:
✅ Hold your phone closer to eye level
✅ Avoid prolonged neck flexion
✅ Take movement breaks every 20–30 minutes
✅ Perform gentle neck and upper back stretches regularly

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we frequently see patients with posture-related neck pain, cervical spondylosis, office-related neck strain, and screen-time-associated spine problems.

Early attention to posture and ergonomics can help reduce long-term stress on the spine and improve overall neck health.

Did you know tight hips and pelvic imbalance can contribute to lower back pain, poor posture, stiffness, and reduced spinal mobility?

Limited hip mobility forces the lower back to compensate, increasing stress on the lumbar spine over time. Simple hip mobility exercises and pelvic tilt movements can help improve posture, reduce back strain, and support a healthier spine.

Prolonged screen time and desk work can contribute to neck pain, upper back stiffness, eye strain, poor posture, and “tech neck syndrome.”

A simple evidence-based habit that helps:
✅ Every 20 minutes
✅ Look 20 feet away

The 20-20-20 rule helps relax neck muscles, reduce screen fatigue, improve posture, and decrease strain on the cervical spine. Simple neck stretches during work breaks can further support spinal health and mobility.

✔️ Hoffmann’s positive sign

featured_reviews.name: Khushboo Doctor
featured_reviews.review_text: I am writing this post in interest of humankind on the basis of real life experience of my mother who had undergone spine surgery under 'WeAreSpine' banner in the hope that Dr. Bhojraj is God of Spine and will truly change our life. Yes, all our lives are drastically changed but with No good & All adversities for lifetime. The most important thing to consider before any surgery is that Whether it is actually needed?? What are all the risks ?? Had ALL THE RISKS been explained to us by the surgeon, we wouldn't had gone for it and my mother would have been living much better life. Its been 3 years, each day we are facing new physical complexities post surgery alongwith existing conditions. I am totally disappointed with Dr Bhojraj for not explaining us all the post surgery possible mishaps (like foot drop, rapid infection as my mother had auto immune disorder) & Mr Premik Nagad who have actually done the surgery as he have actually ruined the spine & nerves and which our family will never ever forget or forgive. I will Never recommend spine surgery to anyone untill THE LAST RESORT and that too after understanding all risks/mishaps.

featured_reviews.name: Sushama Shinde
featured_reviews.review_text:
My father was having the difficulty in walking for past 2-3 months. He could not walk for more than 10 mins sometimes.
That is when we scheduled an appointment with Dr Shekhar Bhojraj.

After physical examination and reviewing the MRI reports, he advised the spine decompression surgery for my father.
After completing the physical fitness checks advised by the team,  my father underwent the proposed surgery on 4th Dec'23.

During his week's stay in hospital, he was made to sit, walk and climb the stairs to which he responded well. All such checks were done before giving the discharge from hospital.

At home, physiotherapy sessions (as advised) are ongoing. He is now getting better day by day. He can now walk straight and I am sure that he will be back on his feet with full strength soon.

I want to thank everyone in Dr Shekhar Bhojraj's team (Dr Pranav Rajendra, Dr Harshad Shah,  Dr Kalpana Shah & Dr Jayesh Bhanushali) for their continuous support throughout this process. The entire team is very prompt in responding and guiding us before as well as post surgery. No words for how grateful we are towards Dr Shekhar Bhojraj and his team for performing this critical surgery successfully and relieving us from the worries.
